name: Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative
jurisdiction: RGGI, a partnership of currently 10 states in the North East of the U.S., covers emissions from the electricity sector in the region.
description: RGGI operates an Auction Reserve Price, a Cost Containment Reserve and an Emission Containment Reserve. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: California Cap-and-Trade Program
jurisdiction: Launched in 2012, the Californian system covers industry and most fossil combustion, accounting for around 80% of total emissions. California linked its system with Québec in January 2014.
description: The Cal C&T operates market stability mechanisms at the upper and the lower price bounds. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: Washington Cap-and-Invest Program
jurisdiction: The program covers around 70% of the state’s emissions, with many of its design elements being similar to those of California’s cap-and-trade program.
description: The program operates market stability mechanisms at the upper and the lower price bounds. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: Washington Cap-and-Invest Program (download)
jurisdiction: The program covers around 70% of the state’s emissions, with many of its design elements being similar to those of California’s cap-and-trade program.
description: The program operates market stability mechanisms at the upper and the lower price bounds. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: California Cap-and-Trade Program (download)
jurisdiction: Launched in 2012, the Californian system covers industry and most fossil combustion, accounting for around 80% of total emissions. California linked its system with Québec in January 2014.
description: The Cal C&T operates market stability mechanisms at the upper and the lower price bounds. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: German National Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The ETS covers all fuel distributors and suppliers and complements the EU ETS. It operates with a fixed price per tCO2 from 2021 to 2025. In 2026, auctions will be introduced.
description: Additional allowances exceeding the cap can be acquired by entities in the fixed-price phase. For more information on the system, see the ICAP Map.

name: European Union Emissions Trading System (until 2018)
jurisdiction: The EU ETS began in 2005 and covers emissions from power, industry, maritime transport, and flights inside the EEA, to and from EU’s nine outermost regions, as well as departing flights from these outermost regions to Switzerland and the UK. This covers around 40% of EU emissions.
description: Since 2019, the EU ETS operates with a Market Stability Reserve (MSR) which addresses market imbalances by temporarily adjusting allowance supply. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: European Union Emissions Trading System (from 2019)
jurisdiction: The EU ETS began in 2005 and covers emissions from power, industry, maritime transport, and flights inside the EEA, to and from EU’s nine outermost regions, as well as departing flights from these outermost regions to Switzerland and the UK. This covers around 40% of EU emissions.
description: Since 2019, the EU ETS operates with a Market Stability Reserve (MSR) which addresses market imbalances by temporarily adjusting allowance supply. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: European Union Emissions Trading System (from 2019, download)
jurisdiction: The EU ETS began in 2005 and covers emissions from power, industry, maritime transport, and flights inside the EEA, to and from EU’s nine outermost regions, as well as departing flights from these outermost regions to Switzerland and the UK. This covers around 40% of EU emissions.
description: Since 2019, the EU ETS operates with a Market Stability Reserve (MSR) which addresses market imbalances by temporarily adjusting allowance supply. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: New Zealand Emissions Trading System (Up to 2023)
jurisdiction: The New Zealand ETS was launched in 2008 and currently covers the power, industry, building, transportation, domestic aviation, waste and forestry (as both a source of emissions and credits) sectors.
description: The NZ ETS operated a Fixed Price Option. From 2021, it was replaced by a Cost Containment Reserve and an Auction Reserve Price that operate for auctions. For more, see the ICAP Map.

name: New Zealand Emissions Trading System (From 2024)
jurisdiction: The New Zealand ETS was launched in 2008 and currently covers the power, industry, building, transportation, domestic aviation, waste and forestry (as both a source of emissions and credits) sectors.
description: The NZ ETS operated a Fixed Price Option. From 2021, it was replaced by a Cost Containment Reserve and an Auction Reserve Price that operate for auctions. For more, see the ICAP Map.

name: Québec Cap-and-Trade System
jurisdiction: Launched in 2012, Québec System covers industry and most fossil combustion representing 80-85% of total emissions. Québec linked its system with California in January 2014.
description: The Québec C&T System operates market stability mechanisms at the upper and the lower price bounds. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: Ontario Cap-and-Trade Program (2017-2018)
jurisdiction: The Ontario program operated from January 2017 till mid-2018. The system was linked to California and Québec and covered industry and most fossil combustion.
description: The Ontario C&T program operated market stability mechanisms at the upper (Cost Containment Reserve) and the lower (Auction Reserve Price) price bound.

name: Nova Scotia Cap-and-Trade Program (2019-2022)
jurisdiction: Nova Scotia’s cap-and-trade program regulated the industry, power, heat (buildings), and transportation sectors and covered more than 80% of GHG emissions in Nova Scotia.
description: The Nova Scotia C&T Program operated market stability mechanisms at the upper (Reserve Account) and the lower (Auction Reserve Price) price bound.

name: China National Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The ETS regulates more than 3,500 companies from the power, steel, cement, and aluminum smelter sectors with annual emissions in excess of 26,000 tCO2.
description: Adjustment mechanisms to prevent abnormal price fluctuations, as well as risk prevention and control mechanisms to prevent market manipulations, are under development. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: Shenzhen (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Shenzhen Pilot covers 40% of CO2 emissions from the power, industry, transport, and buildings sectors.
description: In case of market fluctuations, the Shenzhen government can sell reserve allowances at a fixed price which cannot be traded. They can also buy back up to 10% of total allocation. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Shanghai (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Shanghai Pilot covers 57% of CO2 emissions, from the power, industry, buildings and domestic aviation sectors.
description: The Shanghai Environment and Energy Exchange can take price stabilization measures when the price fluctuates ±10% in one day. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Beijing (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Beijing Pilot covers 45% of CO2 emissions form the power, industry, transport and building sectors.
description: Under pre-determined conditions, the Beijing government can either auction additional allowances or buy back allowances from the market. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Guangdong (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Guangdong Pilot covers 60% of CO2 emissions from the power, industry and domestic aviation sectors.
description: The system has provisions for an Auction Reserve Price. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Tianjin (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Tianjin Pilot covers 55% of CO2 emissions from the power and industry sectors.
description: In case of market fluctuations, the Tianjin government can sell or buy allowances in order to stabilize the market. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Hubei (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Hubei Pilot covers 35% of CO2 emissions from the power and industry sectors.
description: The government can buy and sell allowances to stabilize the market. There is a daily price fluctuation limit of ±10%. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Chongqing (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Chongqing Pilot covers 40% of all GHG emissions from the power and industry sectors.
description: In case of market fluctuations, the Chongqing Carbon Emissions Exchange can take price stabilization measures. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: Fujian (Pilot) Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The Fujian Pilot covers 60% of CO2 emissions from the power, industry and domestic aviation sectors.
description: The system has provisions for price stabilization in case of market fluctuations over a 10 day period, including the option for the government to buy and sell allowances. For more, see ICAP Map.

name: United Kingdom Emissions Trading Scheme
jurisdiction: The UK ETS covers energy-intensive industries, the power sector, and aviation within the UK and EEA, together making up about one third of the UK’s GHG emissions.
description: The UK ETS has a transitional Auction Reserve Price, and a Cost Containment Mechanism for the UK ETS Authority to intervene if prices are elevated for a sustained period.

name: United Kingdom Emissions Trading Scheme (download)
jurisdiction: The UK ETS covers energy-intensive industries, the power sector, and aviation within the UK and EEA, together making up about one third of the UK’s GHG emissions.
description: The UK ETS has a transitional Auction Reserve Price, and a Cost Containment Mechanism for the UK ETS Authority to intervene if prices are elevated for a sustained period.

name: Korean Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: The K-ETS launched in January 2015, covering emitters from power, industry, domestic aviation, waste and buildings, representing 66% of total emissions.
description: In Korea, an Allocation Committee can take quantity- or price-based measures for market stabilization subject to certain criteria. For more information, see the ICAP Map.

name: Switzerland Emissions Trading System
jurisdiction: Starting in 2013, the Swiss ETS covers large emitters from the industrial sector. The Swiss ETS linked to the EU ETS in 2020.
description: No market stability mechanisms. For more information on the system, see the ICAP Map.
